notes:
Stage: procurement for Dedicated capacity. Primary driver: reduce latency and unpredictable cost for reranking + personalization during campaign peaks. Commercial asks: committed min throughput SLA, explicit concurrency caps per model, governed burst policy for marketing events.

Key negotiation points (AE/SE notes):
- Customer insists on a sustained min tokens/sec guarantee for core reranking model: target 1,500 tokens/sec sustained across reserved pool during business hours (08:00-20:00 PT).
- Wants p95 latency SLO <250ms for short-context reranking requests (~64 tokens input, 32 tokens output).
- Concurrency cap request: hard cap of 2,000 concurrent inference sessions for that model with priority queueing for paid routes.
- Burst policy: allow 3x sustained throughput for up to 10 minutes per hour for product launches (cool-off window after bursts). They want clear billing and fallback rules for bursts beyond policy.
- Measurement & verification: want synthetic traffic harness (we provide), shared benchmark logs, and warm-cache preconditioning steps documented. Agreement on measurement windows (5-min rolling, weekly aggregated) is required.
- Fallbacks: automatic routing to smaller quantized model (SLA-adjusted) when sustained load > 120% of reserved baseline; need guarantees about quality delta and roll-back semantics.
- Capacity planning: proposing reserved fleet of 8x H100-class GPUs with autoscaling headroom of +25% (burst nodes) and explicit pre-warm policy for KV-cache to meet p95 targets. Customer requested a cost comparison for A100 vs H100 and for 8 vs 12 node reserve.
- SLA language: request for service credits when min tokens/sec not met for >= 15 consecutive minutes, and definition of force majeure vs capacity shortage. Legal flagged measurement definitions.

Customer quote: "We need predictable throughput — surprises in peak spend or dropped personalization requests cost millions in ad revenue."
